**Continuous 2.38.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.36.0

Headless fetches now follow the Web level. That is the switch 2.36.0 warned about. A prompt that does not fit the model's context window stops and says so, and each model has a context length you can set. A command written for another shell is refused before it runs.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- **Context length.** Models → Configure → Context & cost shows the window in use and lets you raise or lower it. The value is saved as `contextLength` on that model. A length that was nested under `defaultCompletionOptions` is read. When no published window is known, 32,768 is used and the dialog says so.
- **Checkpoints and `/rewind` in the terminal agent.** Before Edit, MultiEdit or Write changes a file, a copy is kept with the session under `~/.continuous/checkpoints/<session id>/`. `/rewind` lists the session's prompts and the files written in each, and can restore the files, rewind the conversation, or both. `r` redoes the last rewind until the agent writes again. `continuous rewind <session> [--to <n>] [--mode files|conversation|both] [--redo]` does the same from a script. A file changed outside the agent since its last write is shown with its line counts and needs `y` or `s`. Files changed by shell commands or MCP tools are not covered. `CONTINUOUS_CHECKPOINTS=off` turns copies off. See `docs/cli/checkpoints.mdx`.
- **Snapshots of files dropped from outside the editor.** A text file dropped on the chat input from Windows File Explorer, Finder, or another window has no path, so it becomes a snapshot chip: its content, read once, marked snapshot. Snapshots refuse secret-named files, files over 200 KB, binary files, and any file in which the secret scanner finds a credential. A message holds at most 20 snapshots and 1 MB of them. A folder becomes snapshots of its text files, two levels deep, skipping `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist` and secret folders.
- **Drop Files for Chat** (VS Code). A view under the chat takes files and folders dropped from the Explorer, editor tabs and the file manager and adds them to the chat input as `@` mentions. From VS Code 1.140, drags no longer reach the chat itself, so the view is shown there by default (`continuous.chatDropZone`: `auto`, `always`, `never`). Items outside the workspace and files that look like secrets are refused with the reason.

### Behaviour changes

- **Headless fetch.** `cn -p` and `cn serve` follow the Web level. At Cautious, only hosts you allowed run. An unlisted public host is refused, and the one-release stderr line is gone. To keep every host running, use `--allow Fetch` or `--policy web=permissive`, or allow the domains in `permissions.yaml`. The start-up line names the Web level, for example `Web Cautious (unattended: only allowed domains)`.
- **A full context window.** When the prompt does not fit, the turn stops and names the prompt size, the window in use, and Models → Configure → Context & cost. A reply that stops because it hit the output limit says that too. Auto-compact still runs when a summary can be saved. When it cannot (a cloud model with no summary ready, or a summary that fails), the turn stops and says the window was full. It does not drop the oldest history and continue with an empty reply.
- **Commands written for another shell.** On Windows PowerShell, a command that will not parse (`&&` or `||`, a heredoc, `/dev/null`, `export`, `NAME=value`, an unclosed quote, and the other parse errors of that kind) is refused before it runs, including at IDGAF. The tool result names the shell, the mistake, a replacement, and says to call again. `rm -rf` stays the destructive safety check: it asks below IDGAF, and at IDGAF it runs unless you turn safety checks on.
- **An exact Always rule** skips only the destructive-command ask and the dependency-change ask. It does not skip a safety refusal, a protected path, a credential, a policy file, or a fetch to a host you have not allowed.
- **The approval card** writes out hidden and direction-changing characters, shows the whole rule and the whole reason on Always allow, and says "command" only for a terminal command. A command cut in the loop inbox says it was cut.
- **Git status in `cn`.** File names in the environment block of the first message have hidden characters removed, and `<` and `>` escaped, so a name cannot close the block.
- The extension badge is the blue-to-purple framed mark.

### Fixes

- A context length set beside `maxTokens` under `defaultCompletionOptions` was ignored. It is read, and saving the context control writes `contextLength` on the model entry, including a `from:` catalog model.

### Upgrade notes

- **Headless fetch.** This is the 2.38 switch named in the 2.36.0 notes. A headless run at Cautious no longer fetches public hosts you have not allowed. `--allow Fetch` or `--policy web=permissive` keeps every host running.
- **Context length.** If a chat stopped with no reply when the window filled, set the length under Models → Configure → Context & cost. 32,768 is only the stand-in used when no window is published for that model.
- **PowerShell.** A command that uses bash syntax is refused with a replacement. Send the replacement as a new call. `rm -rf` is unchanged: it is the safety check, not a parse error.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
